background_notes.justification: Existence of a derivative is differentiability. The difference quotient of a real function has at most one limit: two proposed limits a and b satisfy |a-b|<=|a-Q(h)|+|Q(h)-b|, which tends to zero. Hence the derivative value is the supplied a, here zero. For |h|<tau/2, both tau and tau+h lie in the positive-time domain, so any agreeing total extension has exactly the same difference quotients. This uses no property at time zero.
